evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition EilenbergMoore `(T : C ⟶ C) `{H : @Monad C T} : Category := {| obj := ∃ a : C, @TAlgebra C T H a; hom := fun x y => TAlgebraHom T ``x ``y (projT2 x) (projT2 y); homset := fun _ _ => {| equiv := fun f g => t_alg_hom[f] ≈ t_alg_hom[g] |}; id := fun _ => {| t_alg_hom := id |}; compose := fun _ _ _ f g => {| t_alg_hom := t_alg_hom[f] ∘ t_alg_hom[g] |} |}.
Class TAlgebra `(T : C ⟶ C) `{@Monad C T} (a : C) := { t_alg : T a ~> a; t_id : t_alg ∘ ret ≈ id; t_action : t_alg ∘ fmap t_alg ≈ t_alg ∘ join }.
Class TAlgebraHom `(T : C ⟶ C) `{@Monad C T} (a b : C) (F : TAlgebra T a) (G : TAlgebra T b) := { t_alg_hom : a ~> b; t_alg_hom_commutes : t_alg_hom ∘ t_alg[F] ≈ t_alg[G] ∘ fmap[T] t_alg_hom }.

Definition CoEilenbergMoore : Category := (@EilenbergMoore (C^op) (W^op) H)^op.  (with WCoalgebras_CoEilenbergMoore_Iso : WCoalgebras ≅[Cat] CoEilenbergMoore, line 303 — the dual half of Exercise 5.2.iii)

statement_record.book: For a monad (T, eta, mu) on C, the Eilenberg-Moore category C^T has objects the pairs (A, a : TA -> A) satisfying the unit triangle a . eta_A = id_A and the associativity square a . Ta = a . mu_A (display (5.2.5)); morphisms (A,a) -> (B,b) are the T-algebra homomorphisms f : A -> B with f . a = b . Tf; identities and composition are those of C.

statement_record.book: For a monad (T, eta, mu) on C and any A in C, the free T-algebra on A is (TA, mu_A : T^2 A -> TA), which satisfies the T-algebra axioms by the monad unit and associativity laws; the construction is functorial, giving F^T : C -> C^T with F^T A = (TA, mu_A) and F^T f = Tf, an algebra homomorphism by naturality of mu.
statement_record.intree: EM_Free : C ⟶ EilenbergMoore T with fobj a = (T a; {| t_alg := join |}) and fmap f = {| t_alg_hom := fmap[T] f |}; the algebra axioms are discharged by [join_ret] and [join_fmap_join], the homomorphism square by [join_fmap_fmap] (naturality of mu), and the functor laws by [fmap_id]/[fmap_comp].

statement_record.book: Four identifications of Kleisli categories: (i) for the maybe monad on Set, a Kleisli map A -> B is a partial function, and Kleisli composition is composition of partial functions, so Set^{maybe}_T is isomorphic to Set_partial; (ii) for the free monoid monad, a Kleisli map assigns a list of elements of B to each element of A; (iii) for the state monad (S x -)^S induced by S x (-) -| (-)^S, a Kleisli map A -> B is a function A x S -> B x S; (iv) the Kleisli category of the Giry monad is measurable spaces and Markov kernels.
statement_record.intree: Instance/Sets/Par.v [Part] and Instance/Coq/Par.v [Par]: the categories whose objects are setoids (resp. Coq Types), whose homs A ~> B are the maps A -> option B, whose identity is Some (= ret of the maybe monad) and whose composition is option_bind (= Kleisli composition of the maybe monad).

evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition Kleisli_Adjunction : Kleisli_Free ⊣ Kleisli_Forget := @Build_Adjunction' Kleisli C Kleisli_Free Kleisli_Forget Kleisli_adj_iso _ _.  (Kleisli_adj_iso, line 96: an Isomorphism in Sets between the hom-setoids (Kleisli_Free x ~{Kleisli}~> y) and (x ~> Kleisli_Forget y), both directions the identity map.)
Lemma Kleisli_join_agrees {x : C} : fmap[Kleisli_Forget] (@counit _ _ _ _ Kleisli_Adjunction x) ≈ join[M].
Program Definition Kleisli_Forget : Kleisli ⟶ C := {| fobj := fun x => M x; fmap := fun x y f => join ∘ fmap[M] f |}.  (with Kleisli_Free, line 52: fobj x = x, fmap f = ret ∘ f.)

statement_record.book: For any monad (T, eta, mu) on C there is an adjunction F_T -| U_T between C and the Kleisli category C_T whose underlying monad is (T, eta, mu). F_T is the identity on objects and sends f : A -> B to eta_B . f; U_T sends A to TA and a Kleisli map g : A -> TB to mu_B . Tg. Functoriality and U_T F_T = T are left to Exercise 5.2.v; the adjunction follows from C_T(F_T A, B) iso C(A, TB) iso C(A, U_T B).
statement_record.intree: Kleisli_Free : C ⟶ Kleisli with fobj x = x, fmap f = ret ∘ f; Kleisli_Forget : Kleisli ⟶ C with fobj x = M x, fmap f = join ∘ fmap[M] f; Kleisli_Adjunction : Kleisli_Free ⊣ Kleisli_Forget via Kleisli_adj_iso (identity in both directions, since the two hom-setoids are literally x ~> M y); Kleisli_Monad_agrees : Kleisli_Forget ◯ Kleisli_Free ≈ M; Kleisli_unit_agrees (line 132) : unit ≈ ret[M]; Kleisli_counit_agrees (line 139) : counit ≈ id[M x]; Kleisli_join_agrees : fmap[Kleisli_Forget] (counit) ≈ join[M].
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, and in-tree stronger: the functoriality of F_T and U_T and the identity U_T F_T = T that Riehl defers to Exercise 5.2.v are all proved here (the functor obligations of Kleisli_Free/Kleisli_Forget plus Kleisli_Monad_agrees), and the transposition isomorphism the book asserts is constructed explicitly with both round trips. As in lem9, U_T F_T = T is rendered as a natural isomorphism with identity components rather than a definitional equality.

verifier.notes: All four cited lines verified verbatim against Monad/Kleisli/Adjunction.v (Kleisli_Free 52, Kleisli_Forget 75, Kleisli_adj_iso 96, Kleisli_Adjunction 125, Kleisli_unit_agrees 132, Kleisli_counit_agrees 139, Kleisli_join_agrees 146, Kleisli_Monad_agrees 157). Every obligation is Qed-closed; the adjunction rides the same hom-setoid [Build_Adjunction'] whose triangle identities Theory/Adjunction.v:280/288 derive, so Exercise 5.2.v is genuinely covered. File in _CoqProject (line 264). I added Kleisli_counit_agrees to the intree statement (the classifier listed it only implicitly) and the same natural-iso-vs-equality disclosure as in lem9.
